steps.what: Encourage students to explore learning opportunities and persevere with challenging tasks

tasks.design: The instructor discusses goals, barriers and next steps directly with students. Existing opportunity information in {DOCS} supports encouragement without replacing the relationship.
tasks.previous_blocker: Perseverance depends on confidence, circumstances and trust.
tasks.enabler_now: Accessible resources support discussion but do not establish saved contact time.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding why a student is discouraged and what support will help.
tasks.human_edge: The instructor listens and responds to the individual's situation.
tasks.altitude: Student encouragement and contact time stay unchanged.

reach.task: Coordinate encouragement around a difficult learning task
reach.learn: Adult learning barriers and supportive feedback

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: individual encouragement remains human; a learning-outcome trial does not establish reduced relationship time.

assumptions: Boundary is encouragement and exploration with students, excluding separate course research and admission administration.
Students provide goals and concerns during s1; the instructor checks relevant opportunities there. No structured motivation or readiness score is assumed.
Use existing information resources first; native runtime earns no labour saving. Zero new upkeep because no new tool is introduced.
unknowns: Student goals and available learning pathways
research_questions: Which barriers require personal discussion despite available course information?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0%. Encouragement retains all contact time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Teach adults individually and in groups

steps.what: Instruct students through lectures, discussions and demonstrations

tasks.design: The instructor explains, demonstrates and responds to learners using material in {DOCS}. The lesson interaction stays human, with preparation assessed separately.
tasks.previous_blocker: Teaching requires adapting to what learners understand in the moment.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing material supports explanation without removing the interaction.
tasks.still_hard: Detecting misunderstanding and choosing a useful alternative explanation.
tasks.human_edge: The instructor reads learner responses and adapts the teaching.
tasks.altitude: Teaching responsibility and contact time stay unchanged.

reach.task: Coordinate explanations for learners needing additional practice
reach.learn: Adult learning and language support methods

evidence.claim: Tutor CoPilot's trial reported improved topic mastery with human tutors. It does not establish reduced live teaching time for adult instructors.

assumptions: Boundary is live instruction, excluding planning in task 6826. If one activity falls under both statements, its delivery time is assigned once in roll-ups.
The instructor selects existing material; learners produce questions and responses during s1 before the instructor adapts. No structured understanding flag is assumed.
Test native teaching resources first; existing runtime earns no saving. Zero new upkeep because no teaching assistant is deployed.
unknowns: Teaching format and learner support needs
research_questions: Which teaching adaptations depend on observing learners directly?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0%. Learning-outcome evidence is not treated as a contact-time reduction.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan and conduct balanced learning activities

steps.what: Plan balanced instruction, demonstration and work activities for students

loop.purpose: Draft an activity sequence from instructor-selected objectives and resources
loop.input: Instructor-defined objectives, learner needs, available time and approved source material
loop.output: Draft activity plan with timings, resources and unresolved needs
loop.check: Instructor checks learning purpose, language difficulty, accessibility, practical timing and opportunities to observe, question and investigate
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsuitable activities are replaced manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Existing lesson templates are tried first, but adapting activity wording and sequence to learner needs requires contextual drafting

steps.what: Conduct activities that let students observe, question and investigate

tasks.design: Use existing {LMS} plans and {DOCS} templates before a bounded loop suggests activity wording and sequence. The instructor checks the plan before delivery and retains the whole live activity.
tasks.previous_blocker: Adapting resources into a balanced session takes preparation time.
tasks.enabler_now: A source-bound draft can assist preparation without choosing learner needs or replacing teaching.
tasks.still_hard: Judging difficulty and responding when an activity does not work as expected.
tasks.human_edge: The instructor understands learners and adapts during delivery.
tasks.altitude: Less first-draft planning, with instruction and adaptation retained.

reach.task: Review the alignment of activities with learning objectives

evidence.claim: Easygenerator turns documents or slides into a first course draft; this supports drafting capability, not a measured adult-instructor planning saving.
Model knowledge: the proposed activity-planning shares and review allowance require local measurement.

assumptions: Boundary is activity planning and delivery; overlapping instruction in task 6827 is owned once in team roll-ups.

Within s1 the instructor captures objectives, observed needs, language level, session duration, available materials, accessibility needs and resource versions before drafting. The 22.75 retained hours include capture, design and semantic correction; no free structured learner profile is assumed.
Students produce participation during s2 after instructions, and the instructor adapts within its full 65%. Missing needs or unsuitable drafts return to manual planning.

Test native plans first; existing runtime earns no new saving. Five extra focal hours count template changes, sample plan checks and failed drafts; no additional learner or coordinator work is assumed free.
unknowns: Actual preparation baseline and approved resource coverage
research_questions: Does draft planning save time after need capture and activity correction?

already_counted.description: Need capture, planning and draft meaning checks
Plan approval and full activity delivery

incremental.description: Template changes, plan checks and failed drafts

approvals.approved_version: Exact checked activity plan, objectives, resource versions and learner adaptations reviewed in s2 before delivery; material changes require renewed approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35*0.65+65=87.75; gross 12.25%, net 7.25% after 5 focal upkeep. Range covers failed drafts with zero gain through 8 points of planning removed minus 5 upkeep. All live activity remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assign and grade class work and homework

steps.what: Assign class work and homework with checked answer keys and grading criteria
Read submitted closed-item answers and record the student's selected responses
Grade closed items against the verified answer key and calculate points
Grade open responses and resolve ambiguous or unexpected student answers
Check and return final class work and homework grades

tasks.design: Configure native {LMS} scoring only for closed items with an instructor-verified key and captured responses. The instructor retains assignment selection, response capture, open-response judgement and final grade checks before returning feedback.
tasks.previous_blocker: Closed-item points can be assigned and totalled manually after answers are read.
tasks.enabler_now: Native key-based scoring can repeat fixed comparisons without interpreting open answers.
tasks.still_hard: Unexpected valid answers, partial understanding and useful feedback.
tasks.human_edge: The instructor recognises learning that a fixed key cannot represent.
tasks.altitude: Less mechanical scoring while assessment responsibility remains.

reach.task: Check alignment of fixed keys with learning objectives
reach.learn: Assessment validity and key version control

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: fixed-key closed-item scoring is deterministic, while open-response and final grading judgement remain human. Savings depend on the local item mix.

assumptions: Boundary is assigning and grading work, excluding separate assignment authoring and live teaching. The central scenario has a material closed-item share; wholly open assignments earn no new saving.

In s1 the instructor verifies assignment/version, item IDs, accepted answers, point values, rubric and learning objectives; its full 20% includes key checking and correction. Students produce submitted work after assignment and before s2 under the unchanged baseline; no extra student digitisation task is introduced.

In s2 the instructor produces and captures student ID, assignment version and item/response pairs, including missing or ambiguous response flags; the full 15% remains. Paper responses are entered by the instructor here, not converted free. Ambiguous responses return to s4 manual grading.

Test native LMS scoring first; existing automatic scoring earns no new saving. Seven extra focal hours count key changes, scoring audits and additional exceptions. No new coordinator or student capture work is assumed free.
unknowns: Closed-item share and existing scoring automation
research_questions: Does native scoring save time after paper-response capture, key validation and final checks?

already_counted.description: Final grade approval and feedback return

incremental.description: Key maintenance, scoring audits and additional exceptions

approvals.approved_version: Exact student assignment versions, response captures, key/rubric versions, marks and feedback checked in s5; changes void release approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=20+15+30+10=75; gross 25%, net 18% after 7 focal upkeep. Range covers open-only or already auto-scored work with zero new gain through 15 points of mechanical scoring removed minus 7 upkeep. Key preparation, capture, judgement and feedback remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The instructor retains teaching and assessment judgement while bounded planning drafts and native closed-item scoring offer conditional savings.
reach: Coordinate activity and assessment validity with instructional roles.
role.ambitious_version: More consistent preparation and scoring with learner contact and all first-capture work counted.
